summary: Cincinnati Northern Kentucky International Airport (CVG) sits in Hebron, Kentucky, just across the Ohio River from downtown Cincinnati, serving the tri-state region of Ohio, Kentucky, and Indiana. It operates one of the largest cargo hubs in North America for DHL Aviation and was formerly a major Delta Air Lines hub. The airport features a modern main terminal with two concourses and consistently ranks among the busiest cargo airports in the United States.
faqs:
Q: Where exactly is CVG located?
A: CVG is in Hebron, Kentucky, approximately 13 miles southwest of downtown Cincinnati, Ohio. Despite its name, the airport is on the Kentucky side of the Ohio River.

Q: Is CVG a hub for any major airlines?
A: CVG is the main North American cargo hub for DHL Aviation and offers significant flight options on Delta Air Lines, which maintains a focus city operation there.

Q: How many terminals does CVG have?
A: CVG has a single main terminal building divided into Concourse A and Concourse B, connected by a pedestrian walkway. A separate Concourse C has been largely repurposed.

Q: Does CVG offer nonstop international flights?
A: Yes, CVG offers several nonstop international routes, primarily to leisure destinations in Mexico, the Caribbean, and select European cities, depending on the season.
transport_tips: The airport is easily reached via I-275 from both Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky, with clear signage directing drivers to the terminal. Rideshare services, taxis, and the TANK bus system (route 2X) provide ground transportation options, though a rental car is recommended for exploring the broader region. Parking is available in close-in garages, economy lots, and a remote lot with shuttle service.
local_tip: If you have a long layover, head to the Concourse B food court area for a taste of local Cincinnati favorites like Skyline Chili or Graeter's ice cream, both of which have outposts in the terminal.
